chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hajjaj, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Yahya ibn Talhah, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the minimum that suffices from the Tashahhud. He said, 'The two declarations of faith.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: The testimony or declaration, specifically referring to the sitting portion of the prayer
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَانِ: The two declarations of faith (La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Tashahhud required to validly complete the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the legal minimum (rukun) for the Tashahhud, establishing that the two declarations of faith are sufficient for the validity of the prayer. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is crucial for differentiating between obligatory pillars and recommended supplications, ensuring that the core testimony of Tawhid and Nubuwwah anchors the ritual. The narration underscores the simplicity and accessibility of the prayer's requirements while maintaining theological precision.
